title: Talking About the Future in English | Plans, Dreams & Goals | A2–B1 English Conversation

segments.text: Hello everyone and welcome back to Mr.
segments.ipa: /həˈloʊ ˈɛvriˌwʌn ənd ˈwɛlkəm bæk tu ˈmɪstər/

segments.text: English Channel, where learning English is easy and fun. I'm Emily. Hello Emily. Hi everyone.
segments.ipa: /ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈtʃænəl wɛr ˈlɝnɪŋ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ɪz ˈizi ənd fʌn aɪm ˈɛmɪli həˈloʊ ˈɛmɪli haɪ ˈɛvriˌwʌn/

segments.text: It's great to have you here.
segments.ipa: /ɪts ɡreɪt tu hæv ju hir/

segments.text: Emily, you've got your calendar open.
segments.ipa: /ˈɛmɪli juv ɡɑt jɔr ˈkæləndər ˈoʊpən/

segments.text: Should I be worried?
segments.ipa: /ʃʊd aɪ bi ˈwɝid/

segments.text: Only if you promise to help me move this weekend.
segments.ipa: /ˈoʊnli ɪf ju ˈprɑməs tu hɛlp mi muv ðɪs ˈwiˌkɛnd/

segments.text: We're talking about the future today and I'm making a few weekend plans.
segments.ipa: /wir ˈtɔkɪŋ əˈbaʊt ðə ˈfjutʃər təˈdeɪ ənd aɪm ˈmeɪkɪŋ ə fju ˈwiˌkɛnd plænz/

segments.text: Moving, that's a very dangerous example.
segments.ipa: /ˈmuvɪŋ ðæts ə ˈvɛri ˈdeɪndʒərəs ɪɡˈzæmpəl/

segments.text: But tell me about your actual plans.
segments.ipa: /bʌt tɛl mi əˈbaʊt jɔr ˈæktʃəwəl plænz/

segments.text: What are you going to do this weekend?
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɑr ju ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu du ðɪs ˈwiˌkɛnd/

segments.text: I'm going to visit my sister on Saturday.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu ˈvɪzɪt maɪ ˈsɪstər ɑn ˈsætərdi/

segments.text: We're going to make lunch together, nothing special, just a chance to catch up.
segments.ipa: /wir ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu meɪk lʌntʃ təˈɡɛðər ˈnʌθɪŋ ˈspɛʃəl dʒʌst ə tʃæns tu kætʃ ʌp/

segments.text: That sounds like my kind of Saturday.
segments.ipa: /ðæt saʊndz laɪk maɪ kaɪnd ʌv ˈsætərdi/

segments.text: When you say we're going to make lunch, have you already decided that together?
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju seɪ wir ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu meɪk lʌntʃ hæv ju ɔlˈrɛdi ˌdɪˈsaɪdɪd ðæt təˈɡɛðər/

segments.text: Yep, we talked yesterday.
segments.ipa: /jɛp wi tɔkt ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ/

segments.text: We haven't chosen the food yet, but the plan is there.
segments.ipa: /wi ˈhævənt ˈtʃoʊzən ðə fud jɛt bʌt ðə plæn ɪz ðɛr/

segments.text: What are you going to do?
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɑr ju ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu du/

segments.text: I'm going to clean out my closet.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu klin aʊt maɪ ˈklɑzət/

segments.text: And before you laugh, some of those shirts have been waiting for this moment for years.
segments.ipa: /ənd bɪˈfɔr ju læf sʌm ʌv ðoʊz ʃɝts hæv bɪn ˈweɪtɪŋ fɔr ðɪs ˈmoʊmənt fɔr jɪrz/

segments.text: I wasn't going to laugh, but now I'm picturing the shirts celebrating.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈwɑzənt ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu læf bʌt naʊ aɪm ˈpɪktʃərɪŋ ðə ʃɝts ˈsɛləˌbreɪtɪŋ/

segments.text: Are you really going to do it this Saturday?
segments.ipa: /ɑr ju ˈrɪli ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu du ɪt ðɪs ˈsætərdi/

segments.text: That's the plan, although I said the same thing last month.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ðə plæn ˌɔlˈðoʊ aɪ sɛd ðə seɪm θɪŋ læst mʌnθ/

segments.text: Does going to mean the plan will definitely happen?
segments.ipa: /dʌz ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu min ðə plæn wɪl ˈdɛfənətli ˈhæpən/

segments.text: No, plans can change.
segments.ipa: /noʊ plænz kæn tʃeɪndʒ/

segments.text: It tells us what you've decided or intend to do.
segments.ipa: /ɪt tɛlz ʌs wʌt juv ˌdɪˈsaɪdɪd ɔr ˌɪnˈtɛnd tu du/

segments.text: Your closet might still win this round.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˈklɑzət maɪt stɪl wɪn ðɪs raʊnd/

segments.text: It's a strong opponent, but I've asked my brother to help.
segments.ipa: /ɪts ə strɔŋ əˈpoʊnənt bʌt aɪv æskt maɪ ˈbrʌðər tu hɛlp/

segments.text: He's coming over at 10:00, so now someone else expects me to start.
segments.ipa: /hiz ˈkʌmɪŋ ˈoʊvər æt soʊ naʊ ˈsʌmˌwʌn ɛls ɪkˈspɛkts mi tu stɑrt/

segments.text: Oh, that makes it feel more real.
segments.ipa: /oʊ ðæt meɪks ɪt fil mɔr ril/

segments.text: He's coming over at 10:00 sounds like an arrangement.
segments.ipa: /hiz ˈkʌmɪŋ ˈoʊvər æt saʊndz laɪk æn ərˈeɪndʒmənt/

segments.text: You've agreed on a time together. Exactly.
segments.ipa: /juv əˈɡrid ɑn ə taɪm təˈɡɛðər ɪɡˈzæktli/

segments.text: Like, I'm meeting a friend after work tomorrow.
segments.ipa: /laɪk aɪm ˈmitɪŋ ə frɛnd ˈæftər wɝk təˈmɑˌroʊ/

segments.text: We've already talked and there's probably a place and a time.
segments.ipa: /wiv ɔlˈrɛdi tɔkt ənd ðɛrz ˈprɑbəˌbli ə pleɪs ənd ə taɪm/

segments.text: Right, and we use that same form for things happening now.
segments.ipa: /raɪt ənd wi jus ðæt seɪm fɔrm fɔr θɪŋz ˈhæpənɪŋ naʊ/

segments.text: So, a time phrase helps.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ə taɪm freɪz hɛlps/

segments.text: Tomorrow, on Friday, or next week.
segments.ipa: /təˈmɑˌroʊ ɑn ˈfraɪdi ɔr nɛkst wik/

segments.text: So, if I say, "I'm having dinner with my parents on Sunday," nobody thinks I'm eating dinner during this podcast.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ɪf aɪ seɪ aɪm ˈhævɪŋ ˈdɪnər wɪð maɪ ˈpɛrənts ɑn ˈsʌnˌdeɪ ˈnoʊˌbɑˌdi θɪŋks aɪm ˈitɪŋ ˈdɪnər ˈdʊrɪŋ ðɪs ˈpɔdˌkæst/

segments.text: Unless you're hiding a sandwich under the table.
segments.ipa: /ənˈlɛs jʊr ˈhaɪdɪŋ ə ˈsændwɪtʃ ˈʌndər ðə ˈteɪbəl/

segments.text: But, yes, on Sunday puts that dinner in the future.
segments.ipa: /bʌt jɛs ɑn ˈsʌnˌdeɪ pʊts ðæt ˈdɪnər ɪn ðə ˈfjutʃər/

segments.text: Where are you eating?
segments.ipa: /wɛr ɑr ju ˈitɪŋ/

segments.text: At their house.
segments.ipa: /æt ðɛr haʊs/

segments.text: My dad's cooking, which means he's going to ask everyone whether the food needs more salt before we even sit down.
segments.ipa: /maɪ dædz ˈkʊkɪŋ wɪtʃ minz hiz ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu æsk ˈɛvriˌwʌn ˈwɛðər ðə fud nidz mɔr sɔlt bɪˈfɔr wi ˈivɪn sɪt daʊn/

segments.text: My sister does that, too.
segments.ipa: /maɪ ˈsɪstər dʌz ðæt tu/

segments.text: I'm taking dessert to her house on Saturday, actually.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ˈteɪkɪŋ dɪˈzɝt tu hɝ haʊs ɑn ˈsætərdi ˈækˌtʃuəli/

segments.text: She's making lunch, and I'm bringing something sweet.
segments.ipa: /ʃiz ˈmeɪkɪŋ lʌntʃ ənd aɪm ˈbrɪŋɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ swit/

segments.text: Have you decided what you're bringing?
segments.ipa: /hæv ju ˌdɪˈsaɪdɪd wʌt jʊr ˈbrɪŋɪŋ/

segments.text: Because that sounds like the part of the plan everyone will remember.
segments.ipa: /bɪˈkɔz ðæt saʊndz laɪk ðə pɑrt ʌv ðə plæn ˈɛvriˌwʌn wɪl rɪˈmɛmbər/

segments.text: I'm going to bake an apple pie on Friday evening.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu beɪk æn ˈæpəl paɪ ɑn ˈfraɪdi ˈivnɪŋ/

segments.text: I've already bought the apples.
segments.ipa: /aɪv ɔlˈrɛdi bɑt ðə ˈæpəlz/

segments.text: That's how serious this plan is.
segments.ipa: /ðæts haʊ ˈsɪriəs ðɪs plæn ɪz/

segments.text: You've got ingredients.
segments.ipa: /juv ɡɑt ˌɪnˈɡridiənts/

segments.text: I've got a closet full of excuses.
segments.ipa: /aɪv ɡɑt ə ˈklɑzət fʊl ʌv ɪkskˈjusɪz/

segments.text: Listeners, think about your own weekend.
segments.ipa: /ˈlɪsənərz θɪŋk əˈbaʊt jɔr oʊn ˈwiˌkɛnd/

segments.text: What are you going to do?
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɑr ju ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu du/

segments.text: Try saying one sentence out loud.
segments.ipa: /traɪ ˈseɪɪŋ wʌn ˈsɛntəns aʊt laʊd/

segments.text: It can be small.
segments.ipa: /ɪt kæn bi smɔl/

segments.text: "I'm going to wash my car."
segments.ipa: /aɪm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu wɑʃ maɪ kɑr/

segments.text: Or, "I'm going to call a friend."
segments.ipa: /ɔr aɪm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu kɔl ə frɛnd/

segments.text: And if you've arranged something with another person, try, "I'm meeting my cousin on Saturday."
segments.ipa: /ənd ɪf juv ərˈeɪndʒd ˈsʌmθɪŋ wɪð əˈnʌðər ˈpɝsən traɪ aɪm ˈmitɪŋ maɪ ˈkʌzən ɑn ˈsætərdi/

segments.text: Add the day, so your plan is clear.
segments.ipa: /æd ðə deɪ soʊ jɔr plæn ɪz klɪr/

segments.text: Speaking of clear plans, what happens if your brother calls Saturday morning and says he can't come?
segments.ipa: /ˈspikɪŋ ʌv klɪr plænz wʌt ˈhæpənz ɪf jɔr ˈbrʌðər kɔlz ˈsætərdi ˈmɔrnɪŋ ənd sɛz hi kænt kʌm/

segments.text: Will you still clean the closet?
segments.ipa: /wɪl ju stɪl klin ðə ˈklɑzət/

segments.text: Honestly, my first thought would be, "Great, I'll go back to bed."
segments.ipa: /ˈɑnəstli maɪ fɝst θɔt wʊd bi ɡreɪt aɪl ɡoʊ bæk tu bɛd/

segments.text: But, I'd probably say, "Okay, I'll start without you."
segments.ipa: /bʌt aɪd ˈprɑbəˌbli seɪ ˌoʊˈkeɪ aɪl stɑrt wɪˈθaʊt ju/

segments.text: That "I'll start without you" is a decision you're making in the moment.
segments.ipa: /ðæt aɪl stɑrt wɪˈθaʊt ju ɪz ə dɪˈsɪʒən jʊr ˈmeɪkɪŋ ɪn ðə ˈmoʊmənt/

segments.text: You're responding to something that's just happened. Right.
segments.ipa: /jʊr rɪˈspɑndɪŋ tu ˈsʌmθɪŋ ðæts dʒʌst ˈhæpənd raɪt/

segments.text: I didn't plan for him to cancel.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈdɪdənt plæn fɔr hɪm tu ˈkænsəl/

segments.text: Here's another one.
segments.ipa: /hɪrz əˈnʌðər wʌn/

segments.text: We open your sister's oven, and your beautiful apple pie is completely burned.
segments.ipa: /wi ˈoʊpən jɔr ˈsɪstərz ˈʌvən ənd jɔr ˈbjutəfəl ˈæpəl paɪ ɪz kəmˈplitli bɝnd/

segments.text: That's a terrible future you've created for me, but okay.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ə ˈtɛrəbəl ˈfjutʃər juv kriˈeɪtəd fɔr mi bʌt ˌoʊˈkeɪ/

segments.text: I look at the pie and say, "I'll buy some ice cream instead." Perfect.
segments.ipa: /aɪ lʊk æt ðə paɪ ənd seɪ aɪl baɪ sʌm aɪs krim ˌɪnˈstɛd pərˈfɛkt/

segments.text: A new decision because the situation changed, and I can say, "I'll stop at the store for you."
segments.ipa: /ə nu dɪˈsɪʒən bɪˈkɔz ðə ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən tʃeɪndʒd ənd aɪ kæn seɪ aɪl stɑp æt ðə stɔr fɔr ju/

segments.text: That's an offer.
segments.ipa: /ðæts æn ˈɔfər/

segments.text: An offer I'd happily accept.
segments.ipa: /æn ˈɔfər aɪd ˈhæpəli ækˈsɛpt/

segments.text: You can also ask, "Will you get some chocolate sauce?"
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˈɔlsoʊ æsk wɪl ju ɡɛt sʌm ˈtʃɔklət sɔs/

segments.text: That's a request about what I'd like you to do.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ə rɪˈkwɛst əˈbaʊt wʌt aɪd laɪk ju tu du/

segments.text: Sure, I'll get some.
segments.ipa: /ʃʊr aɪl ɡɛt sʌm/

segments.text: And if I say, "I won't forget it this time," you might hear a promise and a little history.
segments.ipa: /ənd ɪf aɪ seɪ aɪ woʊnt fərˈɡɛt ɪt ðɪs taɪm ju maɪt hir ə ˈprɑməs ənd ə ˈlɪtəl ˈhɪstəri/

segments.text: A very specific history, but that's useful. "I'll help.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈvɛri spəˈsɪfɪk ˈhɪstəri bʌt ðæts ˈjusfəl aɪl hɛlp/

segments.text: I'll call you.
segments.ipa: /aɪl kɔl ju/

segments.text: I won't be late."
segments.ipa: /aɪ woʊnt bi leɪt/

segments.text: People use these to offer help or make promises.
segments.ipa: /ˈpipəl jus ðiz tu ˈɔfər hɛlp ɔr meɪk ˈprɑməsəz/

segments.text: Although "I'll call you" needs action behind it.
segments.ipa: /ˌɔlˈðoʊ aɪl kɔl ju nidz ˈækʃən bɪˈhaɪnd ɪt/

segments.text: Have you ever said that to a friend and then realized a week had passed? I have.
segments.ipa: /hæv ju ˈɛvər sɛd ðæt tu ə frɛnd ənd ðɛn ˈriəˌlaɪzd ə wik hæd pæst aɪ hæv/

segments.text: Now I try to add something specific.
segments.ipa: /naʊ aɪ traɪ tu æd ˈsʌmθɪŋ spəˈsɪfɪk/

segments.text: "I'll call you after dinner tonight."
segments.ipa: /aɪl kɔl ju ˈæftər ˈdɪnər təˈnaɪt/

segments.text: Then I put a reminder on my phone.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn aɪ pʊt ə riˈmaɪndər ɑn maɪ foʊn/

segments.text: That gives the other person a clearer idea of what to expect.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɡɪvz ðə ˈʌðər ˈpɝsən ə ˈklɪrər aɪˈdiə ʌv wʌt tu ɪkˈspɛkt/

segments.text: But what if you want to call and don't know when you'll be free?
segments.ipa: /bʌt wʌt ɪf ju wɑnt tu kɔl ənd doʊnt noʊ wɛn jul bi fri/

segments.text: Then I'd be honest about that.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn aɪd bi ˈɑnəst əˈbaʊt ðæt/

segments.text: Imagine my sister asks, "Are you coming again next weekend?"
segments.ipa: /ˌɪˈmædʒən maɪ ˈsɪstər æsks ɑr ju ˈkʌmɪŋ əˈɡɛn nɛkst ˈwiˌkɛnd/

segments.text: "I'd love to, but I haven't checked my schedule."
segments.ipa: /aɪd lʌv tu bʌt aɪ ˈhævənt tʃɛkt maɪ ˈskɛdʒʊl/

segments.text: That's a tricky little moment.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ə ˈtrɪki ˈlɪtəl ˈmoʊmənt/

segments.text: You want her to know you care, but you don't want to promise a Saturday you might not have. Exactly.
segments.ipa: /ju wɑnt hɝ tu noʊ ju kɛr bʌt ju doʊnt wɑnt tu ˈprɑməs ə ˈsætərdi ju maɪt nɑt hæv ɪɡˈzæktli/

segments.text: I could say, "I might come next Saturday.
segments.ipa: /aɪ kʊd seɪ aɪ maɪt kʌm nɛkst ˈsætərdi/

segments.text: Let me check my schedule."
segments.ipa: /lɛt mi tʃɛk maɪ ˈskɛdʒʊl/

segments.text: She knows I'm interested, and she knows I haven't decided yet.
segments.ipa: /ʃi noʊz aɪm ˈɪntrəstɪd ənd ʃi noʊz aɪ ˈhævənt ˌdɪˈsaɪdɪd jɛt/

segments.text: That feels kinder than saying yes and canceling later.
segments.ipa: /ðæt filz ˈkaɪndər ðæn ˈseɪɪŋ jɛs ənd ˈkænsəlɪŋ ˈleɪtər/

segments.text: Would "Maybe I'll come next Saturday" work there, too? It would.
segments.ipa: /wʊd ˈmeɪbi aɪl kʌm nɛkst ˈsætərdi wɝk ðɛr tu ɪt wʊd/

segments.text: Both leave the possibility open, but I'd add when I'll let her know, so she isn't waiting all week to make lunch plans.
segments.ipa: /boʊθ liv ðə ˌpɑsəˈbɪləˌti ˈoʊpən bʌt aɪd æd wɛn aɪl lɛt hɝ noʊ soʊ ʃi ˈɪzənt ˈweɪtɪŋ ɔl wik tu meɪk lʌntʃ plænz/

segments.text: Especially if apple pie is involved. Mhm.
segments.ipa: /əˈspɛʃli ɪf ˈæpəl paɪ ɪz ˌɪnˈvɑlvd əmhəm/

segments.text: Those little words matter even more with bigger questions, though.
segments.ipa: /ðoʊz ˈlɪtəl wɝdz ˈmætər ˈivɪn mɔr wɪð ˈbɪɡər ˈkwɛstʃənz ðoʊ/

segments.text: Like, "Are you going to move? Oh, yes.
segments.ipa: /laɪk ɑr ju ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu muv oʊ jɛs/

segments.text: A friend asked me that when I mentioned wanting more space.
segments.ipa: /ə frɛnd æskt mi ðæt wɛn aɪ ˈmɛnʃənd ˈwɑntɪŋ mɔr speɪs/

segments.text: Suddenly, an idea sounded like I'd already rented a truck.
segments.ipa: /ˈsʌdənli æn aɪˈdiə ˈsaʊndɪd laɪk aɪd ɔlˈrɛdi ˈrɛntɪd ə trʌk/

segments.text: How did you explain it?
segments.ipa: /haʊ dɪd ju ɪkˈspleɪn ɪt/

segments.text: Because looking at a few houses online can turn into a whole new life in someone else's mind.
segments.ipa: /bɪˈkɔz ˈlʊkɪŋ æt ə fju ˈhaʊsəz ˈɔnˌlaɪn kæn tɝn ˈɪntu ə hoʊl nu laɪf ɪn ˈsʌmˌwʌn ˈɛlsɪz maɪnd/

segments.text: I said I'd like to have a bigger place someday, but I'm not planning to move right now.

segments.ipa: /ə bɪɡ ɡoʊl ɡɛts ˈklɪrər wɛn wi neɪm ðə ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən/

segments.text: So, instead of "I'm going to improve my English, someone might say, I'm going to practice explaining my job for 10 minutes after dinner.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ˌɪnˈstɛd ʌv aɪm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu ˌɪmˈpruv maɪ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈsʌmˌwʌn maɪt seɪ aɪm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu ˈpræktəs ɪkˈspleɪnɪŋ maɪ dʒɑb fɔr ˈmɪnəts ˈæftər ˈdɪnər/

segments.text: Yes, if that fits their evening.
segments.ipa: /jɛs ɪf ðæt fɪts ðɛr ˈivnɪŋ/

segments.text: And if they've got children to feed or a late shift, maybe they practice for 5 minutes before work.
segments.ipa: /ənd ɪf ðeɪv ɡɑt ˈtʃɪldrən tu fid ɔr ə leɪt ʃɪft ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ ˈpræktəs fɔr ˈmɪnəts bɪˈfɔr wɝk/

segments.text: I'm glad you added that.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ɡlæd ju ˈædəd ðæt/

segments.text: Advice can sound easy when you imagine everyone has a quiet house and an empty evening. Exactly.
segments.ipa: /ædˈvaɪs kæn saʊnd ˈizi wɛn ju ˌɪˈmædʒən ˈɛvriˌwʌn hæz ə ˈkwaɪət haʊs ənd æn ˈɛmpti ˈivnɪŋ ɪɡˈzæktli/

segments.text: My sister once tried to study after her kids went to bed.
segments.ipa: /maɪ ˈsɪstər wʌns traɪd tu ˈstʌdi ˈæftər hɝ kɪdz wɛnt tu bɛd/

segments.text: By then, she was falling asleep over the first page.
segments.ipa: /baɪ ðɛn ʃi wɑz ˈfɑlɪŋ əˈslip ˈoʊvər ðə fɝst peɪdʒ/

segments.text: Did she find a better time?
segments.ipa: /dɪd ʃi faɪnd ə ˈbɛtər taɪm/

segments.text: I've tried learning things when I'm exhausted, and mostly I've learned that I'm exhausted.
segments.ipa: /aɪv traɪd ˈlɝnɪŋ θɪŋz wɛn aɪm ɪɡˈzɔstɪd ənd ˈmoʊstli aɪv lɝnd ðæt aɪm ɪɡˈzɔstɪd/

segments.text: She started listening during her lunch break twice a week.
segments.ipa: /ʃi ˈstɑrtɪd ˈlɪsənɪŋ ˈdʊrɪŋ hɝ lʌntʃ breɪk twaɪs ə wik/

segments.text: She could manage that without losing sleep, so she kept doing it.
segments.ipa: /ʃi kʊd ˈmænədʒ ðæt wɪˈθaʊt ˈluzɪŋ slip soʊ ʃi kɛpt ˈduɪŋ ɪt/

segments.text: That makes me think about money, too.
segments.ipa: /ðæt meɪks mi θɪŋk əˈbaʊt ˈmʌni tu/

segments.text: Someone might want to travel or take a course, but even a small monthly payment can be difficult. It can.
segments.ipa: /ˈsʌmˌwʌn maɪt wɑnt tu ˈtrævəl ɔr teɪk ə kɔrs bʌt ˈivɪn ə smɔl ˈmʌnθli ˈpeɪmənt kæn bi ˈdɪfəkəlt ɪt kæn/

segments.text: We shouldn't pretend every dream has an easy solution.
segments.ipa: /wi ˈʃʊdənt priˈtɛnd ˈɛvəri drim hæz æn ˈizi səˈluʃən/

segments.text: Sometimes the useful question is, what can I try with what I have right now?
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz ðə ˈjusfəl ˈkwɛstʃən ɪz wʌt kæn aɪ traɪ wɪð wʌt aɪ hæv raɪt naʊ/

segments.text: Like checking whether the library has a free conversation group, or asking a friend to practice a short phone call together once a week.
segments.ipa: /laɪk ˈtʃɛkɪŋ ˈwɛðər ðə ˈlaɪbrɛˌri hæz ə fri ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃən ɡrup ɔr ˈæskɪŋ ə frɛnd tu ˈpræktəs ə ʃɔrt foʊn kɔl təˈɡɛðər wʌns ə wik/

segments.text: And for my train trip with mom, the next step is checking actual ticket prices.
segments.ipa: /ənd fɔr maɪ treɪn trɪp wɪð mɑm ðə nɛkst stɛp ɪz ˈtʃɛkɪŋ ˈæktʃəwəl ˈtɪkət ˈpraɪsəz/

segments.text: If the long trip costs too much, we could visit a nearby town.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ðə lɔŋ trɪp kɑsts tu mʌtʃ wi kʊd ˈvɪzɪt ə ˈnɪrˈbaɪ taʊn/

segments.text: Would that feel disappointing, though?
segments.ipa: /wʊd ðæt fil ˌdɪsəˈpɔɪntɪŋ ðoʊ/

segments.text: You've been picturing several days away.
segments.ipa: /juv bɪn ˈpɪktʃərɪŋ ˈsɛvrəl deɪz əˈweɪ/

segments.text: I think it's okay to admit the smaller version might feel different. It would.
segments.ipa: /aɪ θɪŋk ɪts ˌoʊˈkeɪ tu ədˈmɪt ðə ˈsmɔlər ˈvɝʒən maɪt fil ˈdɪfərənt ɪt wʊd/

segments.text: I'd probably be sad about changing it, but I'd still enjoy sitting beside her,
segments.ipa: /aɪd ˈprɑbəˌbli bi sæd əˈbaʊt ˈtʃeɪndʒɪŋ ɪt bʌt aɪd stɪl ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ˈsɪtɪŋ bɪˈsaɪd hɝ/

segments.text: looking out the window, and having time to talk.
segments.ipa: /ˈlʊkɪŋ aʊt ðə ˈwɪndoʊ ənd ˈhævɪŋ taɪm tu tɔk/

segments.text: That helps you see what you care about most.
segments.ipa: /ðæt hɛlps ju si wʌt ju kɛr əˈbaʊt moʊst/

segments.text: I had a friend who wanted a big birthday party, then realized he mostly wanted his brother there.
segments.ipa: /aɪ hæd ə frɛnd hu ˈwɔntɪd ə bɪɡ ˈbɝθˌdeɪ ˈpɑrti ðɛn ˈriəˌlaɪzd hi ˈmoʊstli ˈwɔntɪd hɪz ˈbrʌðər ðɛr/

segments.text: Was his brother able to come?
segments.ipa: /wɑz hɪz ˈbrʌðər ˈeɪbəl tu kʌm/

segments.text: Sometimes the person we want to see has plans and problems we don't know about.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz ðə ˈpɝsən wi wɑnt tu si hæz plænz ənd ˈprɑbləmz wi doʊnt noʊ əˈbaʊt/

segments.text: He couldn't make that weekend.
segments.ipa: /hi ˈkʊdənt meɪk ðæt ˈwiˌkɛnd/

segments.text: They had dinner together a month later.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ hæd ˈdɪnər təˈɡɛðər ə mʌnθ ˈleɪtər/

segments.text: My friend still had his party, but he stopped treating one date as his only chance.
segments.ipa: /maɪ frɛnd stɪl hæd hɪz ˈpɑrti bʌt hi stɑpt ˈtritɪŋ wʌn deɪt æz hɪz ˈoʊnli tʃæns/

segments.text: That's something I'm learning, too.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ˈsʌmθɪŋ aɪm ˈlɝnɪŋ tu/

segments.text: A delayed plan can hurt, especially when other people seem to be moving ahead with everything they wanted.
segments.ipa: /ə dɪˈleɪd plæn kæn hɝt əˈspɛʃli wɛn ˈʌðər ˈpipəl sim tu bi ˈmuvɪŋ əˈhɛd wɪð ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ ðeɪ ˈwɔntɪd/

segments.text: Yeah, you hear someone's buying a house or changing careers, and suddenly your own ordinary Tuesday feels like evidence that you're behind.
segments.ipa: /jæ ju hir ˈsʌmˌwʌnz ˈbaɪɪŋ ə haʊs ɔr ˈtʃeɪndʒɪŋ kərˈɪrz ənd ˈsʌdənli jɔr oʊn ˈɔrdəˌnɛri ˈtuzdi filz laɪk ˈɛvədəns ðæt jʊr bɪˈhaɪnd/

segments.text: Even though you don't know the whole story.
segments.ipa: /ˈivɪn ðoʊ ju doʊnt noʊ ðə hoʊl ˈstɔri/

segments.text: That person might be excited about the house and worried about the payments at the same time.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ˈpɝsən maɪt bi ɪkˈsaɪtəd əˈbaʊt ðə haʊs ənd ˈwɝid əˈbaʊt ðə ˈpeɪmənts æt ðə seɪm taɪm/

segments.text: Or starting a new career at 40 and feeling nervous beside someone who started at 25.
segments.ipa: /ɔr ˈstɑrtɪŋ ə nu kərˈɪr æt ənd ˈfilɪŋ ˈnɝvəs bɪˈsaɪd ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu ˈstɑrtɪd æt/

segments.text: Looking confident doesn't mean they know exactly what's coming. True.
segments.ipa: /ˈlʊkɪŋ ˈkɑnfədənt ˈdʌzənt min ðeɪ noʊ ɪɡˈzæktli wʌts ˈkʌmɪŋ tru/

segments.text: I'd like us to give ourselves room to say, "I'm still figuring it out."
segments.ipa: /aɪd laɪk ʌs tu ɡɪv aʊərˈsɛlvz rum tu seɪ aɪm stɪl ˈfɪɡjərɪŋ ɪt aʊt/

segments.text: You can be unsure and still make a thoughtful decision this week.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn bi ənˈʃʊr ənd stɪl meɪk ə ˈθɔtfəl dɪˈsɪʒən ðɪs wik/

segments.text: What's yours going to be?
segments.ipa: /wʌts jʊrz ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu bi/

segments.text: We've talked about a lot of future plans, but I'm curious which one will actually get a place on your calendar.
segments.ipa: /wiv tɔkt əˈbaʊt ə lɑt ʌv ˈfjutʃər plænz bʌt aɪm ˈkjʊriəs wɪtʃ wʌn wɪl ˈækˌtʃuəli ɡɛt ə pleɪs ɑn jɔr ˈkæləndər/

segments.text: I'm going to call Mom tomorrow and ask which days work for her.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu kɔl mɑm təˈmɑˌroʊ ənd æsk wɪtʃ deɪz wɝk fɔr hɝ/

segments.text: Then we'll look at the prices together.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn wil lʊk æt ðə ˈpraɪsəz təˈɡɛðər/

segments.text: What about you?
segments.ipa: /wʌt əˈbaʊt ju/

segments.text: I'll text my brother after we finish here and confirm Saturday morning.
segments.ipa: /aɪl tɛkst maɪ ˈbrʌðər ˈæftər wi ˈfɪnɪʃ hir ənd kənˈfɝm ˈsætərdi ˈmɔrnɪŋ/

segments.text: My closet has enjoyed a long, peaceful life.
segments.ipa: /maɪ ˈklɑzət hæz ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪd ə lɔŋ ˈpisfəl laɪf/

segments.text: Things are about to change.
segments.ipa: /θɪŋz ɑr əˈbaʊt tu tʃeɪndʒ/

segments.text: I hope the shirts are ready.
segments.ipa: /aɪ hoʊp ðə ʃɝts ɑr ˈrɛdi/

segments.text: And to everyone listening, think of one future conversation you could have this week,
segments.ipa: /ənd tu ˈɛvriˌwʌn ˈlɪsənɪŋ θɪŋk ʌv wʌn ˈfjutʃər ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃən ju kʊd hæv ðɪs wik/

segments.text: even a very small one.
segments.ipa: /ˈivɪn ə ˈvɛri smɔl wʌn/

segments.text: You could ask a friend, "What are you doing this weekend?"
segments.ipa: /ju kʊd æsk ə frɛnd wʌt ɑr ju ˈduɪŋ ðɪs ˈwiˌkɛnd/

segments.text: Or share something you'd like to try.
segments.ipa: /ɔr ʃɛr ˈsʌmθɪŋ jud laɪk tu traɪ/

segments.text: You don't need a perfect five-year answer.
segments.ipa: /ju doʊnt nid ə pərˈfɛkt ˈfaɪvˌjɪr ˈænsər/

segments.text: We hope you'll have more chances to use your English, meet people, and talk about the things that matter to you.
segments.ipa: /wi hoʊp jul hæv mɔr ˈtʃænsəz tu jus jɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ mit ˈpipəl ənd tɔk əˈbaʊt ðə θɪŋz ðæt ˈmætər tu ju/

segments.text: Thanks for spending this time with us.
segments.ipa: /θæŋks fɔr ˈspɛndɪŋ ðɪs taɪm wɪð ʌs/

segments.text: And thanks for bringing your hopes and questions along.
segments.ipa: /ənd θæŋks fɔr ˈbrɪŋɪŋ jɔr hoʊps ənd ˈkwɛstʃənz əˈlɔŋ/

segments.text: It's been lovely talking with you.
segments.ipa: /ɪts bɪn ˈlʌvli ˈtɔkɪŋ wɪð ju/

segments.text: We'll see you next time on Mr. English Channel.
segments.ipa: /wil si ju nɛkst taɪm ɑn ˈmɪstər ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈtʃænəl/

segments.text: Keep practicing, take care of yourself, and remember, learning English is easy and fun. Goodbye, everyone. Goodbye.
